chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ayyub from Abu Ubaydah who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! Inform me of something that I may benefit from.' So he said, 'O Abu Ubaydah, remember death often, for a person does not remember death often but that he detaches himself from the [yearnings of the material] world.'

key_terms.جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ: may I be your ransom (a common phrase of respect)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of frequently remembering death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the remembrance of death (*dhikr al-mawt*) as the primary key to asceticism (*zuhd*), a concept central to Shia spiritual ethics. This practice is not merely contemplative but serves as a practical mechanism to detach the heart from worldly distractions, aligning the believer’s focus with the eternal realm. The tradition underscores the scholarly view that mortality awareness is the foundation of moral discipline and spiritual purification.
